deep.reconstruction:
Folio 150v is almost empty. It holds only a heading and the first words of a sentence that is never finished. The rest of the sheet shows faint mirror-image bleed-through from the recto (150r). That bleed-through is the derivation transcribed as the previous page and is not new text.

The text reads: 'Ausdruck der Grössen X_ι, Y_ι, Z_ι, wenn diese Kräfte nur von gegenseitigen Anziehungen und Abstossungen der materiellen Punkte herrühren. Die Componenten der Kräfte welche …' In English: 'Expression of the quantities X_ι, Y_ι, Z_ι when these forces arise only from mutual attractions and repulsions of the material points. The components of the forces which …'

Context: on the preceding page (Molecularmechanik, I) Riemann wrote Newton's equations m_ι d²x_ι/dt² = X_ι for a free system. He then recast them as a minimum principle on the accelerations, Σ m_ι |a_ι − F_ι/m_ι|², which is Gauss's principle of least constraint for an unconstrained system. Here he starts the next step: specialising the forces to pairwise central interactions.

The intended continuation is my reconstruction and is not on the page. Write r_{ιι'} = sqrt((x_ι−x_{ι'})² + (y_ι−y_{ι'})² + (z_ι−z_{ι'})²). The force exerted on m_ι by m_{ι'} has magnitude f_{ιι'}(r_{ιι'}) along the line joining them, so X_ι = Σ_{ι'≠ι} f_{ιι'}(r_{ιι'}) (x_{ι'} − x_ι)/r_{ιι'}, and similarly for Y_ι and Z_ι. Equivalently, X_ι = −∂U/∂x_ι with U = Σ_{pairs} F_{ιι'}(r_{ιι'}) and F' = −f, with the sign convention that f > 0 means attraction. Presumably this was meant to feed back into the minimum principle (constraint function) of the previous page, or into energy and momentum theorems. None of this is actually written on the page.
errors: No derivation is present, so there are no mathematical errors. The sentence breaks off after 'welche'.

results.what: Programme heading: express the force components X, Y, Z of a point system whose forces are only mutual attractions and repulsions, i.e. central pairwise forces.
results.modern_name: Central two-body forces / pairwise potential forces
results.usually_credited_to: Newton; systematised by Laplace, Poisson, Gauss and others (18th–early 19th c.)

deep.surprise_reason: The page has only a heading and an unfinished sentence announcing the standard central-force expression for a system of particles. There is no mathematical content.

checkable.sympy: x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2=symbols('x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2'); F=Function('F'); r=sqrt((x1-x2)**2+(y1-y2)**2+(z1-z2)**2); simplify(-diff(F(r),x1) - (-diff(F(r),r)*(x1-x2)/r)) == 0
checkable.asserts: The force on point 1 derived from a pair potential F(r12) is directed along the line joining the points, with magnitude −F'(r).
Mutual central forces are equal and opposite (action = reaction), so their sum over the pair vanishes.

transcription_corrections: The subscripts on X, Y, Z appear to be ι (iota), i.e. X_ι, Y_ι, Z_ι, matching the Σ m_ι notation of the previous page, rather than the numeral 1.
Riemann writes 'Grössen', 'Abstossungen' with 'ss'; the transcription's 'ß' is a normalisation.
The faint mirrored text in the right half of the sheet is bleed-through from folio 150r and should not be transcribed as part of 150v.
